svg.title: Zane Wang — building tools that make AI coding agents more reliable
svg.desc: A terminal window whose login banner is a pixel-art sunset over a skyline drawn from the past year of GitHub contributions: one building per week, one window per day, lit on days with contributions. Below it: 12 pull requests merged into 10 upstream projects, the tools Zane maintains, and how he works.

g.text: building tools that make AI coding agents more reliable
↑ the past year of GitHub activity: one building per week, one window per day, lit on days I contributed
# 10 bug fixes and 2 small features, each merged by that project's maintainers
Allow header no longer lists HEAD twice after merge
pre-1970 SQLite REAL datetimes no longer off by 2 s
custom model as new-chat default no longer fails
RegExp content-type parsers no longer miss matches
.catch() gets the original input, as documented
falsy combine() results memoized, not recomputed
# links to every PR: open "Full profile" below this image
local-first memory for coding agents; Markdown is the record
↳ 11k lines of Go, 10k lines of tests, CI, release builds for 3 OSes
hands work from a lead model to cheaper ones via resumable specs
↳ ships with a small-sample evaluation, including the run where it lost
Claude Code plugin: investigate, test, verify, open the PR
↳ the workflow below as a command, hooks, and file-backed state
# earlier experiments, hackathon-scale and labeled as such: FireSight · dipole · postprism
gather evidence before forming a theory
scope it, pick the reversible path
write the failing test, then the fix
PR → CI → watch it in production
# the code behind this: dev-orchestrator (lifecycle) · handoff (delegation)

text.tspan: and my AI answers from public context
· at most 3 a day per person
